newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to propose food distribution plan to U.N..
newsitem.headline: Iraq to propose food distribution plan to U.N..

text.p: Iraq will present a new food and medicine distribution plan under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, the Iraqi News Agency said on Sunday.
"The Iraqi government will submit during the coming period a distribution plan in order that all measures of renewing the oil-for-food agreement are ready," INA said in a dispatch from New York.

The United Nations on Wednesday renewed the deal that began last December 10. Under the pact Iraq can sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy humanitarian goods needed because of the U.N. sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
INA said Iraq's U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon and U.N. Undersecretary-General Hans Corell exchanged letters on Saturday extending the programme for another 180 days starting on Sunday.

The United States and Britain supported the renewal but expressed concerns about the distribution of supplies. During the first six-month period, 151 U.N. observers supervised the arrival, storage and distribution of food. Iraq has accused Washington of delaying supplies.
